scope: macOS arm64, DuckDB 2.0.0 Node SDK, synthetic in-memory store
checks: Enrolled but unaudited connections cannot use native persisted read/write aliases, including empty reads.
A single audited generation authorizes bounded/native/scalable queries, reads, schema registration, put and patch.
Explicit invalidation and new unknown connections reject the same cached prepared query.
Invalidated replay after raw mutation cannot advance the clock.
Activation independently rejects retained carrier corruption, native history corruption, orphan interval provenance and missing clock.
Repair and a new full audit restore the same cached answer.
Persisted and temporary SQL macros cannot impersonate the native owner check or authorize an unaudited write.
Activation rejects tampered or missing managed view definitions using the pinned DuckDB parse tree.
Activation rejects a mismatch between retained usage and retained rows; repairing usage restores authorization.

earlier_runs.finding: The test pointed at the wrong companion artifact directory; no audit or persisted query ran.
A corrupted native-owned row could be detected by either retained or history proof. The corrected test corrupts a legacy row outside entity_history to isolate the retained proof.

The first one-strategy artifact allowed persisted macros to shadow unqualified companion calls. An unaudited schema definition was accepted. Explicit system catalog calls resolved the real companion and rejected the unaudited context.
The system-qualified native helpers and canonical catalog checks passed before storage accounting equality was added.
